title: CSS Transitions
definition: A CSS module that lets you create gradual transitions between the values of specific CSS properties.
simpleExplanation: If you hover over a button and it turns from Blue to Red instantly, it feels jarring. A Transition tells the browser: 'When the color changes, don't do it instantly. Take 0.3 seconds to smoothly blend the blue into red.'
realWorldExample: Almost every button on the modern web. When you hover your mouse over it, it smoothly lights up or slightly grows in size.

basic: What are the two most common properties provided to the `transition` shorthand?
intermediate: Why is it better to put the `transition` property on the base element rather than the `:hover` state?

answers.question: Common properties?
answers.answer: The property to animate (e.g., `background-color` or `all`) and the duration (e.g., `0.3s`).

answers.question: Why on the base element?
answers.answer: If you put `transition` on the `:hover` state, it will smoothly transition WHEN you hover. But when you move your mouse away (un-hover), it instantly snaps back because the transition rule no longer applies. Putting it on the base element ensures it is smooth in BOTH directions.
